purpose: Test whether the native HUGSIM dynamic contribution changes a fixed target AD beyond reset sensitivity and moves its planning output toward the matched real-source response. This is a one-window receiver-consequence bridge, not a sensor-equivalence or AD-correctness test.

selection_basis: four frames are the minimum history used by the frozen SparseDrive adapter
the frame spacing is approximately 0.5 seconds in official source metadata
frame 44 has prior source-side dynamic support in CAM_FRONT_LEFT
the receiver outputs for this three-way comparison were not inspected before freezing this record
selection.split_boundary: Only the endpoint is reused from the prior reader-declared source-support audit. The three preceding receiver warm-up frames are not claimed to form an independently held-out four-frame test sequence.

conditions.real: official HUGSIM sample source RGB at frames 26, 32, 38 and 44
conditions.factual: HUGSIM exact-source-pose RGB with the released native dynamic enabled at every selected frame
conditions.static_control: the same HUGSIM exact-source-pose RGB with each selected frame's dynamics dictionary cleared
conditions.static_leakage_boundary: Prior inspection found person-like residual content in the static reconstruction. Static control therefore means native-dynamic-path omitted, not actor-free.

held_fixed: source camera intrinsics and relative poses
source-derived command and future ego-motion reference
SparseDrive checkpoint, config, adapter and temporal reset procedure

receiver.role: fixed target AD whose response is compared; not simulator truth
receiver.repeat_design: Each condition is run twice after an independent temporal reset. Cross-condition distances use all four 2-by-2 reset pairings.

measurements.primary_output: SparseDrive native final planning trajectory at fully warmed frame 44
secondary_descriptive: signed final right and forward differences
fixed-mode candidate differences if mode selection changes
measurements.repeat_envelope: maximum within-condition endpoint plan ADE across real, factual and static-control independent resets
measurements.native_effect: factual-versus-static plan ADE over all four reset pairings
measurements.real_gap_factual: real-versus-factual plan ADE over all four reset pairings
measurements.real_gap_static: real-versus-static plan ADE over all four reset pairings

decision_rules.claim: The native dynamic contribution causes a receiver response beyond reset sensitivity.
decision_rules.accepted: minimum factual-static ADE across reset pairings is greater than the maximum within-condition repeat ADE
decision_rules.rejected: maximum factual-static ADE does not exceed the maximum within-condition repeat ADE

decision_rules.claim: Adding the native dynamic moves the receiver plan toward the real-source plan.
decision_rules.accepted: maximum real-factual ADE is strictly below minimum real-static ADE
decision_rules.rejected: maximum real-static ADE is strictly below minimum real-factual ADE
decision_rules.down-weighted: the real-factual and real-static ADE ranges overlap

decision_rules.claim: The endpoint result is not a planning-mode-selection artifact.
decision_rules.accepted: the selected mode is identical across real, factual and static control for both resets
decision_rules.down-weighted: mode changes but fixed-mode decomposition preserves the primary direction
decision_rules.rejected: mode changes and fixed-mode decomposition contradicts or cannot support the primary direction

strongest_allowed_claim: For this one natural-actor history and frozen SparseDrive receiver, enabling the native HUGSIM dynamic path does or does not create a repeat-resolved planning response in the direction of the matched real-source response.
claims_to_reject: SparseDrive is a correct driving policy or a source of ground truth.
The static control is an actor-free world.
A plan moving toward the real-input plan proves photometric, semantic, geometric or sensor equivalence.
One endpoint establishes general HUGSIM credibility, closed-loop safety or receiver-independent validity.
